steps.title: Somatotypes
steps.body: A system of classifying body types based on physical characteristics. There are three main somatotypes: endomorph, mesomorph and ectomorph. Most people are a blend of all three, with one type being dominant.

steps.title: Endomorph
steps.body: A somatotype characterised by a high proportion of body fat, a wide waist and hips, and a rounded, soft body shape. Endomorphs tend to store fat easily and find it difficult to lose weight.

steps.title: Mesomorph
steps.body: A somatotype characterised by a muscular, athletic build with broad shoulders, narrow waist and low body fat. Mesomorphs gain muscle easily and have a naturally strong, powerful physique.

steps.title: Ectomorph
steps.body: A somatotype characterised by a lean, thin build with low body fat and low muscle mass. Ectomorphs are typically tall and slender with narrow shoulders and a fast metabolism.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe the three somatotypes and give a sporting example for each. | Explain why an endomorph is well-suited to being a rugby prop forward. | Why is an ectomorph the ideal somatotype for a marathon runner?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know all three somatotypes with their key physical characteristics Give a specific sport AND position example for each somatotype Remember: most athletes are a BLEND - always mention the dominant type plus others Always explain WHY a somatotype is suited to a sport, not just that it is Endomorph = fat/wide, Mesomorph = muscular/athletic, Ectomorph = lean/thin When comparing sports positions, explain how the somatotype blend varies
